title: Development and Evaluation of a Pump Sampler for Small‐Bodied Fish, Suitable in Challenging Environments
content:
ABSTRACT

Collecting live juvenile and small-bodied fish is challenging due to their fragility and environmental factors like turbidity and flow rates, which affect the use of methods such as electrofishing or fine-meshed nets. Plankton pumps offer a viable alternative, reducing inaccuracies and damage to organisms. This research introduces a fish sampler based on plankton pumps for studying juvenile fish migration in tidal rivers. We tested the pump sampler at the Bergenmeersen flood area, Belgium, connected to the Scheldt River. This pump sampler, designed for relatively high-flow, high-turbidity conditions, consists of a centrifugal pump, suction filter, vacuum ejector, sampler inlet, and detachable box filter. Efficiency and mortality rates were compared to conventional plankton nets through 13 measurements from April to September 2022. Simultaneous samplings during inflow periods showed that the pump sampler offered similar capture efficiency and resulted in lower fish mortality, proving it to be effective and fish-friendly. Unlike traditional nets, which clogged and required frequent emptying, this pump sampler allowed mid-sampling cleaning without interruption, enhancing sampling continuity and convenience while simultaneously improving fish survival. It also enhanced operator safety by enabling bank-side operation.
